items.passage:
A machine shop log records four job runs that used the same coolant.
One: a titanium run at Kestrel Works on nights, switched 4 March, measured by 29 March, ran 6 minutes shorter than the same run last quarter; machinist Draska.
Two: a titanium run at Kestrel Works on nights, switched 5 March, measured by 30 March, ran 4 minutes shorter than the same run last quarter; machinist Draska.
Every logged run was cut on a machine hired from outside, carrying its own tooling. Each shop moved its machines to a coated carbide insert grade that quarter. Cycle times cover the pieces cut on the new coolant throughout, and the whole of each run was cut on the new coolant.
Three: a titanium run at Kestrel Works on nights, switched 6 March, measured by 31 March, ran 7 minutes shorter than the same run last quarter; machinist Draska.
Four: a titanium run at Kestrel Works on nights, switched 7 March, measured by 28 March, ran 5 minutes shorter than the same run last quarter; machinist Draska.
Entries were made in the shop ledger in minutes and initialled by the foreman.
items.notes: Check that all four runs share one value on workshop, alloy, shift and machinist. The closer names the shop's insert refit and then blocks it: every logged run was cut on a machine hired from outside, so the refit cannot reach the runs, and the tail rules out anything else. That is what makes a quarter-over-quarter cycle-time comparison adequate here.

items.confound_note: All four runs are titanium at Kestrel Works on the night shift inside one quarter, and one retooling covers every case at once. The mid-passage line records that "Each shop moved its machines to a coated carbide insert grade that quarter" and that "every logged run was cut on one of those machines", putting the new inserts in every run logged. A coated grade cuts at higher speed than an uncoated one and moves cycle time by itself, and each run is compared against the same run last quarter, cut on the earlier grade, rather than against a run on the same inserts over the same period. The 4 to 7 minute reductions cannot be separated from the retooling.
items.notes: Cases are byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. The insert refit works as a single confound ONLY because the four runs share workshop and shift, and it reaches them because every run was cut on one of the refitted machines. Both closer clauses are reused elsewhere in the family - the refit fact also appears in coherent_true and the scope clause also appears in diverse_true - so the contrast is a conjunction, not a vocabulary difference.

items.confound_note: In cases one, three and four the shorter cycle time was recorded before the coolant was switched: 29 March precedes 4 May, and 30 September precedes 5 October. Three quarters of the evidence therefore describes runs that had already sped up when the treatment was introduced, so it cannot be evidence for the treatment. The one remaining case is not enough by itself.
items.notes: The closer shares its fact clause with diverse_true and its scope clause with coherent_true, so neither clause marks the label; the conditions are verbatim identical to diverse_true. The flaw lives only in the switch dates of cases one and three, which a bag-of-ngrams classifier cannot see because the month tokens are all still ordinary dates. A single shared confound is unavailable here: four workshops, four alloys, four shifts and four quarters share no common event.
